page.heading: About the app
page.subtitle: Household Budget helps you plan spending: every category has a weekly, monthly and yearly limit, and the app shows how much of it you have already spent. It was built as an engineering thesis and shows an application made of microservices.

steps.title: Getting started
steps.subtitle: Six steps from creating an account to your first summaries.

account.title: Create an account or use a demo one
account.text: Demo accounts come with data from recent months, which goes back to its starting state every 2 hours.

categories.title: Add categories and limits
categories.text: For example Food or Transport. Every category has a weekly, monthly and yearly limit.

expenses.title: Record expenses
expenses.text: An expense has a name, amount, date and category. Payments that are still to come are marked as planned.

budgets.title: Keep an eye on budgets
budgets.text: Budgets for upcoming periods are created from the category limits, and you can change the amount of any period.

dashboard.title: Check the Dashboard
dashboard.text: Week, month and year summaries, spending by category and recent transactions in one place.

settings.title: Adjust your account
settings.text: Change your sign-in details, theme and language, or clear your data to start over.

architecture.title: How it works
architecture.subtitle: The frontend talks to a single BFF layer, which calls independent microservices, each with its own database.
architecture.diagramLabel: System diagram: browser, BFF, three microservices and their databases

frontend.title: Frontend
frontend.caption: React, TypeScript and Material UI in the browser

bff.title: BFF (Backend for Frontend)
bff.caption: Spring Boot: JWT sign-in and combining data from the services

gateway.title: A single entry point
gateway.text: The browser only knows the BFF. It checks the JWT token, passes the user's id to the services through OpenFeign and combines their answers, for example budgets with the sum of expenses.

data.title: Distributed data
data.text: Expenses are split into two shards by user. Writes go to the primary instance, reads to the replica. Services see the tables of other databases through postgres_fdw.

security.title: Security
security.text: Passwords are stored as BCrypt hashes, and the services check that an operation concerns the signed-in user. On demo accounts changing sign-in details and deleting the account are blocked.

technologies.title: Technologies
technologies.subtitle: The main libraries and tools used in the project.

mui.name: Material UI
mui.text: Components, light and dark theme, tables (MUI X DataGrid) and date pickers.

charts.name: Chart.js
charts.text: Dashboard charts with colours that stay readable for colour-blind users.

spring.name: Java 21 + Spring Boot 3
spring.text: Four REST services: BFF, users, budgets and expenses.

jpa.name: Spring Data JPA / Hibernate
jpa.text: Data access and filtered search (Criteria API).

feign.name: OpenFeign
feign.text: Calls from the BFF to the microservices.

openapi.name: OpenAPI (springdoc)
openapi.text: API documentation and a TypeScript client generated from it.

postgres.name: PostgreSQL 16
postgres.text: A separate database for every service.

sharding.name: Sharding and replication
sharding.text: Two expense shards, each with a streaming replica for reads.

fdw.name: postgres_fdw
fdw.text: Tables of other databases visible locally, without copying the data.

docker.name: Docker Compose
docker.text: The whole environment: six databases, four services and the frontend.

deploy.name: GitHub Actions
deploy.text: Automatic deployment after every change on the main branch.
